anc27_neighborhood_water_point.what: Man-made pit sunk into the ground to tap groundwater.
anc27_neighborhood_water_point.earliestOnPage: Around 8400 BC, Cyprus well 116 at Kissonerga-Mylouthkia, called the oldest reliably dated well.

anc27_market_stall_arcade.what: Covered public walkway or portico in ancient Greek architecture, often around marketplaces; its name inspired Stoicism.

anc27_city_granary_district.what: Above-ground building for storing harvested grain or seeds, protecting them from pests, floods, and weather while helping prevent mold.
anc27_city_granary_district.earliestOnPage: Oldest found date to 9500 BC, Pre-Pottery Neolithic A settlements in the Jordan Valley.

anc27_potters_wheel_pivot_bearing.what: Machine that shapes clay into round ware by throwing.
anc27_potters_wheel_pivot_bearing.earliestOnPage: Mid-5th millennium BC Cucuteni-Trypillia wheel in western Ukraine.

anc27_processional_avenue.what: Main street of ancient Rome from the Capitoline through the Forum to the Colosseum.
anc27_processional_avenue.earliestOnPage: Eastern stretch rerouted after the Great Fire of AD 64.

anc27_raised_public_causeway.what: Raised track, road, or railway on an embankment over wet ground or water, built of earth, masonry, or wood.
anc27_raised_public_causeway.earliestOnPage: Sweet Track, Somerset Levels, England, built 3807 or 3806 BC (Neolithic age)

anc27_stone_street_curb.what: Edges between raised sidewalks or medians and roadways; the page covers their history, functions, types and materials.
anc27_stone_street_curb.earliestOnPage: Ancient Pompeii had curbs (undated); widespread use began in 18th-century London.

anc27_street_rainwater_channel.what: Collecting and storing rainwater for irrigation, domestic supply and recharge.
anc27_street_rainwater_channel.earliestOnPage: Late 4000 BC: cisterns already essential to dry-land water management.

anc27_public_assembly_plaza.what: A rectangular central Rome plaza ringed by ancient government buildings, once the hub for commerce, justice, politics, and religion.
anc27_public_assembly_plaza.earliestOnPage: 8th century BC, Rome: early finds at the Regia, Comitium, and Vulcanal mark its shift from cemetery to public site.

anc27_public_fountain_courtyard.what: Overview of decorative water structures, from ancient functional basins to modern jet and musical fountains, and how their water supply shaped their design.
anc27_public_fountain_courtyard.earliestOnPage: Carved stone basin, c. 700 BC, Lagash, ancient Sumer (modern Iraq)

anc27_residential_street_block.what: Roman multi-storey apartment blocks that housed most urban residents, with shops on the ground floor and rented flats above.
anc27_residential_street_block.earliestOnPage: 2nd century AD: Insula dell'Ara Coeli, Rome (the example the page gives).

anc27_boundary_inscription_marker.what: Robust physical markers, often stones, that identify the start of a land boundary or a change in its direction.

anc27_civic_boundary_wall.what: Fortifications guarding settlements against attackers, ranging from simple palisades to massive curtain walls, sometimes marking regional borders.
anc27_civic_boundary_wall.earliestOnPage: Jericho, West Bank: wall surrounding it as early as the 8th millennium BC.

anc27_stone_paved_processional_road.what: Main street of ancient Rome from the Capitoline through the Forum to the Colosseum.
anc27_stone_paved_processional_road.earliestOnPage: Eastern stretch rerouted after the Great Fire of AD 64.

anc27_cobblestone_urban_street.what: Natural building material of rounded stones used for roads and buildings, common in Europe for millennia and especially in medieval times.
anc27_cobblestone_urban_street.earliestOnPage: Ancient times, England: flat stones set on edge, predating granite setts by over a thousand years.

anc27_andean_highland_road_segment.what: Pre-Columbian South America's largest transport network, about 40,000 km, with engineered roads, bridges, and relay stations; no wheels.
anc27_andean_highland_road_segment.earliestOnPage: Tiwanaku culture, around Lake Titicaca (Peru/Bolivia), 6th-12th centuries CE, built part of the network.

anc27_persian_royal_road_station.what: Ancient highway rebuilt for trade and fast communication by the Achaemenid Empire, linking Susa and Sardis via relay couriers.
anc27_persian_royal_road_station.earliestOnPage: 5th century BCE, reorganized by the Achaemenid Empire between Susa and Sardis; Assyrian-era western sections possibly older.

anc27_river_ford_stone_bed.what: Shallow river or stream crossing that people, horses, or vehicles can wade; cheap but may be impassable in floods.

anc27_raised_marsh_causeway.what: Raised track, road, or railway on an embankment over wet ground or water, built of earth, masonry, or wood.
anc27_raised_marsh_causeway.earliestOnPage: Sweet Track, Somerset Levels, England, built 3807 or 3806 BC (Neolithic age)

anc27_timber_planked_swamp_road.what: Neolithic oak-plank causeway across the Somerset Levels, England, on crossed pegs over marsh.
anc27_timber_planked_swamp_road.earliestOnPage: Post Track, 3838 BC, underlying parts of the Sweet Track.

anc27_stone_step_mountain_road.what: Pre-Columbian South America's largest transport network, about 40,000 km, with engineered roads, bridges, and relay stations; no wheels.
anc27_stone_step_mountain_road.earliestOnPage: Tiwanaku culture, around Lake Titicaca (Peru/Bolivia), 6th-12th centuries CE, built part of the network.

anc27_mountain_pass_switchback.what: Road bend with a very acute inner angle requiring about a 180-degree turn.

anc27_pack_animal_caravan_track.what: Group travelling together, often on trade expeditions in deserts and on the Silk Road.
anc27_pack_animal_caravan_track.earliestOnPage: Emperor Wu of Han sent some of the first Silk Road caravans in the 2nd century BCE.

anc27_desert_waystation.what: Historic roadside and urban inns along trade routes in the Islamic world, offering lodging, animal stabling, and merchandise storage.
anc27_desert_waystation.earliestOnPage: Early 8th century, Qasr al-Hayr al-Sharqi, Umayyad complex, Syria (oldest identified Islamic caravanserai)

anc27_roadside_milestone.what: Numbered marker along roads or canals showing distance or position.
anc27_roadside_milestone.earliestOnPage: Milion monument in Constantinople, early 4th century AD.

anc27_rural_footpath_bridge.what: Bridge designed solely for pedestrians, from stepping stones and boardwalks to steel structures.
anc27_rural_footpath_bridge.earliestOnPage: Prehistoric timber piles near Lake Zurich (Seedamm) dated to 1523 BC.

anc27_road_embankment_retainer.what: Rigid structure holding back soil so ground sits at different levels.

anc27_curb_cut_water_crossing.what: Edges between raised sidewalks or medians and roadways; the page covers their history, functions, types and materials.
anc27_curb_cut_water_crossing.earliestOnPage: Ancient Pompeii had curbs (undated); widespread use began in 18th-century London.

anc27_rutted_cart_track.what: Two-wheeled vehicle pulled by people or draught animals.
anc27_rutted_cart_track.earliestOnPage: Earliest known wheels c. 3400-3000 BC; the page does not date the earliest carts.

anc27_roadside_shelter_station.what: Historic roadside and urban inns along trade routes in the Islamic world, offering lodging, animal stabling, and merchandise storage.
anc27_roadside_shelter_station.earliestOnPage: Early 8th century, Qasr al-Hayr al-Sharqi, Umayyad complex, Syria (oldest identified Islamic caravanserai)

anc27_roman_road_foundation.what: Infrastructure built from about 300 BC to move armies, officials, mail and trade.

anc27_timber_pile_bridge.what: Bridge designed solely for pedestrians, from stepping stones and boardwalks to steel structures.
anc27_timber_pile_bridge.earliestOnPage: Prehistoric timber piles near Lake Zurich (Seedamm) dated to 1523 BC.

anc27_timber_bridge_diagonal_brace.what: Bridge whose superstructure is a truss of connected straight elements.
anc27_timber_bridge_diagonal_brace.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (1820 lattice-truss patent only).

anc27_woven_grass_suspension_bridge.what: Primitive bridge whose deck rests on two parallel cables anchored at each end.
anc27_woven_grass_suspension_bridge.earliestOnPage: Oldest known suspension bridge reported from Central American ruins, 7th century (page statement).

anc27_cantilevered_log_bridge.what: Bridge whose projecting cantilevers are supported at one end, using beams, trusses or box girders.
anc27_cantilevered_log_bridge.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (page: 1866 Gerber hinged girder; Hassfurt Bridge 1867 = first modern cantilever bridge).

anc27_stone_ford_bank_retaining_apron.what: Rigid structure holding back soil so ground sits at different levels.

anc27_corbel_stone_bridge.what: Stepped courses of stone or brick offset inward to span an opening; a false arch needing thick walls and abutment.
anc27_corbel_stone_bridge.earliestOnPage: Newgrange passage tomb, built between 3200 and 2500 BC during the Neolithic period, has an intact corbel vault.

anc27_barrel_vault_stone_bridge.what: Bridge with abutments at each end shaped as a curved arch, passing load partly as horizontal thrust.
anc27_barrel_vault_stone_bridge.earliestOnPage: Mycenaean Arkadiko Bridge, Greece, about 1300 BC.

anc27_aqueduct_arch_bridge.what: Constructed watercourse carrying water from a source to a distant distribution point.
anc27_aqueduct_arch_bridge.earliestOnPage: Around 2000 BC the Minoans likely first used aqueducts (page statement).

anc27_masonry_multiarch_viaduct.what: Bridge carried on a row of arches, piers or columns across valleys, roads or water.

anc27_reed_raft_floating_bridge.what: Bridge supported by floats or shallow-draft boats carrying a continuous deck.
anc27_reed_raft_floating_bridge.earliestOnPage: Shi Jing attributes one to King Wen in the 11th century BC; Needham suggests 9th-8th century BC.

anc27_anchored_barge_bridge.what: Bridge supported by floats or shallow-draft boats carrying a continuous deck.
anc27_anchored_barge_bridge.earliestOnPage: Shi Jing attributes one to King Wen in the 11th century BC; Needham suggests 9th-8th century BC.

anc27_log_bundle_floating_bridge.what: Bridge supported by floats or shallow-draft boats carrying a continuous deck.
anc27_log_bundle_floating_bridge.earliestOnPage: Shi Jing attributes one to King Wen in the 11th century BC; Needham suggests 9th-8th century BC.

anc27_stone_bridge_pier.what: Upright support for an arch or bridge, often square or rectangular in section.

anc27_riverbank_bridge_abutment.what: Substructure at the ends of a bridge span or dam that supports it and resists lateral earth pressure.

anc27_timber_trestle_crossing.what: Bridge of several short spans held up by closely spaced frames.
anc27_timber_trestle_crossing.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (earliest dated structure 1867).

anc27_catenary_rope_crossing.what: Primitive bridge whose deck rests on two parallel cables anchored at each end.
anc27_catenary_rope_crossing.earliestOnPage: Oldest known suspension bridge reported from Central American ruins, 7th century (page statement).

anc27_narrow_gorge_footbridge.what: Bridge designed solely for pedestrians, from stepping stones and boardwalks to steel structures.
anc27_narrow_gorge_footbridge.earliestOnPage: Prehistoric timber piles near Lake Zurich (Seedamm) dated to 1523 BC.

anc27_mountain_cable_traverse.what: Primitive bridge whose deck rests on two parallel cables anchored at each end.
anc27_mountain_cable_traverse.earliestOnPage: Oldest known suspension bridge reported from Central American ruins, 7th century (page statement).

anc27_roman_pontoon_crossing.what: Bridge supported by floats or shallow-draft boats carrying a continuous deck.
anc27_roman_pontoon_crossing.earliestOnPage: Shi Jing attributes one to King Wen in the 11th century BC; Needham suggests 9th-8th century BC.

anc27_papyrus_reed_raft.what: Ancient reed-built watercraft such as boats and rafts, still used in places.
anc27_papyrus_reed_raft.earliestOnPage: Remains from H3 site, Kuwait, about 7,000 years old = oldest known reed boat remains.

anc27_pitch_sealed_hull_seam.what: Material that seals joints or seams against leakage; also the act of applying it.

anc27_fire_hollowed_canoe_blank.what: Boat made from a hollowed-out tree, also called a logboat or monoxylon.

anc27_twin_hull_river_raft.what: Watercraft with two parallel hulls of equal size, giving stability without ballast.
anc27_twin_hull_river_raft.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (page: first documented European twin-hulled craft 1662)

anc27_sewn_plank_riverboat.what: Flat-bottomed boat without its own propulsion, usually towed or pushed on waterways.

anc27_pole_propelled_flatboat.what: Rectangular flat-bottomed boat used on US inland waterways.

anc27_paddle_propelled_canoe.what: Hand-held tool with a long handle and flat blade that pushes water to propel a boat.

anc27_river_trading_scow.what: Flat-bottomed boat without its own propulsion, usually towed or pushed on waterways.

anc27_mediterranean_merchant_galley.what: Oar-propelled ship used for war, trade and piracy, developed in the Mediterranean.
anc27_mediterranean_merchant_galley.earliestOnPage: Relief of king Sahure at Abusir (2487-2475 BC) shows oared vessels.

anc27_red_sea_plank_boat.what: Wooden boat whose planks are stitched or bound with fibre rope, tendons or flexible wood.
anc27_red_sea_plank_boat.earliestOnPage: Abydos boats, earliest dated c. 3050 BC.

anc27_sewn_plank_ocean_ship.what: Wooden boat whose planks are stitched or bound with fibre rope, tendons or flexible wood.
anc27_sewn_plank_ocean_ship.earliestOnPage: Abydos boats, earliest dated c. 3050 BC.

anc27_peg_fastened_ship_hull.what: Joint connecting two pieces of wood with a hole and a projecting tongue.
anc27_peg_fastened_ship_hull.earliestOnPage: Structure from Hemudu culture, Zhejiang, China, about 7,000 years ago.

anc27_austronesian_outrigger_vessel.what: Watercraft with lateral support floats attached to the hull, developed by Austronesian peoples.
anc27_austronesian_outrigger_vessel.earliestOnPage: Around 3000 BC (Austronesian expansion); outrigger origin estimated about 1500 BCE.

anc27_austronesian_double_canoe.what: Watercraft with lateral support floats attached to the hull, developed by Austronesian peoples.
anc27_austronesian_double_canoe.earliestOnPage: Around 3000 BC (Austronesian expansion); outrigger origin estimated about 1500 BCE.

anc27_pacific_voyaging_canoe.what: Traditional wayfinding using stars, swells, winds and birds for long Pacific voyages.
anc27_pacific_voyaging_canoe.earliestOnPage: Lapita culture mid-2nd millennium BC; spread to Tonga and Samoa 1300-900 BC.

anc27_lapstrake_wooden_boat.what: Boatbuilding in which hull plank edges overlap and are fastened through the overlap.
anc27_lapstrake_wooden_boat.earliestOnPage: c. 310-320 AD, Bjorke and Nydam boats (page statement).

anc27_ancient_dhow_hull.what: Traditional sailing vessels with lateen or settee sails of the Red Sea and Indian Ocean.
anc27_ancient_dhow_hull.earliestOnPage: Most scholars date its origin to India, 600 BC-600 AD.

anc27_south_asian_stitched_boat.what: Wooden boat whose planks are stitched or bound with fibre rope, tendons or flexible wood.
anc27_south_asian_stitched_boat.earliestOnPage: Abydos boats, earliest dated c. 3050 BC.

anc27_cargo_amphora_stowage.what: Ceramic storage and transport jar with two handles, used for wine, oil or garum.
anc27_cargo_amphora_stowage.earliestOnPage: Amphorae from about 4800 BC at Banpo, China (page statement).

anc27_star_rising_navigation.earliestOnPage: Lapita culture mid-2nd millennium BC; spread to Tonga and Samoa 1300-900 BC.

anc27_polynesian_star_compass.earliestOnPage: Lapita culture mid-2nd millennium BC; spread to Tonga and Samoa 1300-900 BC.

anc27_stick_wave_chart.what: Marshallese navigation charts of coconut-frond midribs and shells mapping ocean swell patterns around islands.
anc27_stick_wave_chart.earliestOnPage: A public notice by a missionary in 1862 first revealed the system (documentation date, not origin).

anc27_monsoon_trade_passage.what: Seasonal reversal of winds and rainfall driven by annual shifts of the Intertropical Convergence Zone.

anc27_ditch_and_rampart_fort.what: Broad-topped embankment or wall forming a fortified site defensive boundary, of earth or masonry.

anc27_city_wall_battlement.what: Low parapet with regular gaps (crenels) for shooting, with solid merlons for cover.
anc27_city_wall_battlement.earliestOnPage: Earliest confirmed example at the Buhen fortress, Egypt, Middle Kingdom.

anc27_timber_palisade_wall.what: Row of closely placed high vertical stakes or trunks used as a fence or defensive wall.

anc27_fortified_hilltop_citadel.what: Defensive core within a settlement, usually a castle or fortress, the last line of defence.

anc27_moated_city_fortification.what: A deep ditch around castles or towns, wet or dry, that slowed sieges by blocking siege engines and funneling attackers.
anc27_moated_city_fortification.earliestOnPage: Ancient Egyptian fortresses such as Buhen in Nubia (undated).

anc27_fortified_grain_store.what: Above-ground building for storing harvested grain or seeds, protecting them from pests, floods, and weather while helping prevent mold.
anc27_fortified_grain_store.earliestOnPage: Oldest found date to 9500 BC, Pre-Pottery Neolithic A settlements in the Jordan Valley.

anc27_watchtower_signal_beacon.what: Tower with lamps and lenses emitting light as a navigational aid for maritime pilots.
anc27_watchtower_signal_beacon.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (page cites the Cordouan predecessor, 880s).

anc27_sea_harbour_chain_barrier.what: Obstacle strung across navigable water, floating boom or submerged chain, to control navigation.
anc27_sea_harbour_chain_barrier.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (page: siege of Damietta 1218-19).

anc27_stone_bastion_precursor.what: Angular structure projecting from a fortification wall with flanks covering the walls.

anc27_siege_protective_mantlet.what: Portable shield or wall that stops projectiles.

anc27_timber_shield_wall.what: Military formation of soldiers shoulder to shoulder with overlapping shields.
anc27_timber_shield_wall.earliestOnPage: Stele of the Vultures shows Sumerian soldiers in shield-wall formation, third millennium BC.

anc27_mobile_field_palisade.what: Row of closely placed high vertical stakes or trunks used as a fence or defensive wall.

anc27_fortified_caravan_waystation.what: Group travelling together, often on trade expeditions in deserts and on the Silk Road.
anc27_fortified_caravan_waystation.earliestOnPage: Emperor Wu of Han sent some of the first Silk Road caravans in the 2nd century BCE.

anc27_frontier_signal_post.what: Intentionally conspicuous device that draws attention to a location.
anc27_frontier_signal_post.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (page: Byzantine beacon system, 9th century)

anc27_roman_marching_camp.what: Latin term for Roman military camps and forts of legions and auxiliaries.

anc27_medicinal_herb_garden.what: Private plot near the house growing edible and some medicinal plants for household use.
anc27_medicinal_herb_garden.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (16th-century writing cited)

anc27_pharmacist_drying_rack.what: Historical practitioner who compounds and supplies drugs.
anc27_pharmacist_drying_rack.earliestOnPage: Babylonian apothecary profession "at least 2600 BC" (clay tablet medical texts).

anc27_herbal_grinding_mortar.what: Bowl and club-shaped tool for crushing and grinding.
anc27_herbal_grinding_mortar.earliestOnPage: Ancient mortars and pestles in Southwest Asia dated to about 35000 BC (page statement).

anc27_plant_poultice_cloth.what: Soft damp (often heated) medicinal mass spread on the skin to ease inflammation or pain.
anc27_plant_poultice_cloth.earliestOnPage: Sumerian tablets c. 2200 BCE describe poultices made with milk and beer.

anc27_resin_wound_dressing.what: Soft damp (often heated) medicinal mass spread on the skin to ease inflammation or pain.
anc27_resin_wound_dressing.earliestOnPage: Sumerian tablets c. 2200 BCE describe poultices made with milk and beer.

anc27_honey_wound_dressing.what: Soft damp (often heated) medicinal mass spread on the skin to ease inflammation or pain.
anc27_honey_wound_dressing.earliestOnPage: Sumerian tablets c. 2200 BCE describe poultices made with milk and beer.

anc27_apothecary_remedy_jar.what: Historical practitioner who compounds and supplies drugs.
anc27_apothecary_remedy_jar.earliestOnPage: Babylonian apothecary profession "at least 2600 BC" (clay tablet medical texts).

anc27_ayurvedic_herbal_formulation.what: Traditional medicine system of the Indian subcontinent; the page describes it as pseudoscientific.
anc27_ayurvedic_herbal_formulation.earliestOnPage: Terminology and concepts in the Buddhist Canon from the middle of the first millennium BCE.

anc27_sacred_healing_sanctuary.what: Healing temple of ancient Greece and the Hellenistic and Roman world dedicated to Asclepius.

anc27_ancient_chinese_materia_medica.what: Practice drawn from traditional Chinese medicine, largely a 20th-century construct; herbal remedies, acupuncture, massage.
anc27_ancient_chinese_materia_medica.earliestOnPage: Traces of healing activity in the Shang dynasty, 14th-11th centuries BCE.

anc27_bronze_surgical_probe.what: Medical device used in surgery to cut, modify tissue or give access.

anc27_iron_medical_forceps.what: Handheld hinged instrument for grasping objects, used in biology and medicine.

anc27_bone_surgical_spatula.what: Flat flexible broad-bladed tool for mixing, spreading and lifting substances.

anc27_bronze_wound_needle.what: Long slender hand tool with a point and an eye for thread.
anc27_bronze_wound_needle.earliestOnPage: Bone awls at Blombos Cave, 73,000-70,000 years ago (awls, not needles).

anc27_linen_medical_bandage.what: Strip of material that supports a wound or holds a dressing in place.

anc27_bone_setting_splint.what: Device holding a displaced or injured body part in place.
anc27_bone_setting_splint.earliestOnPage: Splint use dated to 1500 BC, but the page flags the claim as needing a citation - treat as unverified.

anc27_traction_bone_splint.what: Device holding a displaced or injured body part in place.
anc27_traction_bone_splint.earliestOnPage: Splint use dated to 1500 BC, but the page flags the claim as needing a citation - treat as unverified.

anc27_ancient_dental_drill.what: Branch of medicine covering teeth, gums and mouth.
anc27_ancient_dental_drill.earliestOnPage: A 2017 study suggested Neanderthals used rudimentary dentistry tools 130,000 years ago.

anc27_dental_extraction_forceps.what: Handheld hinged instrument for grasping objects, used in biology and medicine.

anc27_obstetric_birthing_stool.what: Device supporting a woman upright during childbirth; backless version is a birth stool.
anc27_obstetric_birthing_stool.earliestOnPage: Egypt, 1450 BCE: queen giving birth on a stool at the Birth House at Luxor.

anc27_midwife_delivery_kit.what: Profession covering pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care.
anc27_midwife_delivery_kit.earliestOnPage: Ebers Papyrus, 1900-1550 BCE, shows midwifery as a recognised female occupation in Egypt.

anc27_medical_cupping_vessel.what: Alternative treatment using heated cups for skin suction; the page says no conclusive evidence supports claimed benefits.

anc27_surgery_instrument_case.what: Medical device used in surgery to cut, modify tissue or give access.

anc27_ancient_trepanation_drill.what: Surgical procedure drilling or scraping a hole in the skull, one of the oldest known surgeries.
anc27_ancient_trepanation_drill.earliestOnPage: French burial ground c. 6500 BCE with 40 of 120 skulls trepanned.

anc27_ear_examination_probe.what: Medical device used in surgery to cut, modify tissue or give access.

anc27_roman_surgical_scalpel.what: Small very sharp cutting instrument for surgery and dissection.
anc27_roman_surgical_scalpel.earliestOnPage: Obsidian scalpels older than 2100 BC from a Bronze Age settlement in Turkey.

anc27_horizon_solar_marker.what: Study of how past peoples understood and used the sky.
anc27_horizon_solar_marker.earliestOnPage: Sumerian observation of Canopus at Eridu over six thousand years ago.

anc27_sunrise_observation_pillar.what: Study of how past peoples understood and used the sky.
anc27_sunrise_observation_pillar.earliestOnPage: Sumerian observation of Canopus at Eridu over six thousand years ago.

anc27_solstice_alignment_avenue.what: Moment the Sun reaches its most northerly or southerly point relative to the celestial equator.
anc27_solstice_alignment_avenue.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (Latin term in late Roman Republic).

anc27_equinox_shadow_marker.what: Moment the Sun appears directly above the equator, twice a year.
anc27_equinox_shadow_marker.earliestOnPage: 45 BC: Julius Caesar set 25 March as the spring equinox in the Julian calendar.

anc27_ancient_star_catalogue.earliestOnPage: Babylonian catalogues in the Kassite period, c. 1531 - c. 1155 BC.

anc27_babylonian_planetary_almanac.what: Early Mesopotamian recording of celestial objects using a base-60 system.

anc27_egyptian_decanal_star_clock.what: 36 star groups of ancient Egyptian astronomy dividing the ecliptic into 10-degree parts for timekeeping.
anc27_egyptian_decanal_star_clock.earliestOnPage: 21st century BC, used as a sidereal clock by at least the Ninth or Tenth Dynasty.

anc27_lunar_phase_calendar_tablet.what: Calendar whose months track the Moon phase cycle.
anc27_lunar_phase_calendar_tablet.earliestOnPage: Samuel L. Macey dates earliest Moon use for time-keeping to 28,000-30,000 years ago.

anc27_eclipse_omen_observation_record.what: Event in which one body is obscured by another body shadow or by passing between it and the viewer.
anc27_eclipse_omen_observation_record.earliestOnPage: Syrian clay tablet records a solar eclipse of 5 March 1223 BC.

anc27_sidereal_observation_register.earliestOnPage: Babylonian catalogues in the Kassite period, c. 1531 - c. 1155 BC.

anc27_stone_gnomon_shadow_chart.what: The part of a sundial that casts a shadow; also a measuring concept.
anc27_stone_gnomon_shadow_chart.earliestOnPage: Painted stick from Taosi, China, 2300 BC, oldest known gnomon in China.

anc27_solar_calendar_circle.what: Calendar keyed to the Sun, tracking seasons or the Sun place among the stars.

anc27_lunar_calendar_intercalation_table.what: Calendar combining lunar months with the solar year, adding intercalary months.
anc27_lunar_calendar_intercalation_table.earliestOnPage: Chinese record dates to the Zhou dynasty, 1050-771 BC.

anc27_armillary_ring_sphere.what: Model of the sky built from rings representing celestial coordinate lines.
anc27_armillary_ring_sphere.earliestOnPage: 4th century BC per Needham (Shi Shen, Gan De); Cullen disputes, dating it to the 1st century BC.

anc27_ancient_celestial_globe.what: Instrument showing apparent positions of stars on a sphere.
anc27_ancient_celestial_globe.earliestOnPage: 2nd-century AD Farnese Atlas depicts a globe; earliest surviving globe made 1080-1085.

anc27_bronze_astronomical_sight_tube.what: Classical astronomical and surveying sighting instrument on a stand.

anc27_ancient_zenith_viewing_well.what: Study of how past peoples understood and used the sky.
anc27_ancient_zenith_viewing_well.earliestOnPage: Sumerian observation of Canopus at Eridu over six thousand years ago.

anc27_greek_celestial_sphere.what: Abstract sphere concentric with Earth used to specify positions in the sky.

anc27_hellenistic_astronomical_dioptra.what: Classical astronomical and surveying sighting instrument on a stand.

anc27_sexagesimal_calculation_tablet.what: Base-60 numeral system from the Sumerians, still used for time and angles.
anc27_sexagesimal_calculation_tablet.earliestOnPage: Origin dated to the 3rd millennium BC (late 3rd millennium weight units).

anc27_babylonian_multiplication_table.what: Table defining multiplication for an algebraic system, traditionally memorised in arithmetic.
anc27_babylonian_multiplication_table.earliestOnPage: Chinese decimal table on bamboo strips, about 305 BC.

anc27_egyptian_fraction_table.what: Finite sum of distinct unit fractions.
anc27_egyptian_fraction_table.earliestOnPage: not stated (Middle Kingdom origin undated; Liber Abaci 1202).

anc27_mesopotamian_field_area_tablet.what: Mesopotamian mathematics recorded in cuneiform on clay tablets.
anc27_mesopotamian_field_area_tablet.earliestOnPage: Tablets from about 2000 BC with a doubling-time interest exercise.

anc27_surveyor_geometry_diagram.what: Roman surveying instrument with a rotating cross and plumb bobs for right angles and straight lines.
anc27_surveyor_geometry_diagram.earliestOnPage: Not firmly dated; may have originated in Mesopotamia or Greece before the 4th century BC.

anc27_euclidean_compass_and_straightedge.what: Building lengths, angles and figures with an unmarked straightedge and compass (Euclid postulates).
anc27_euclidean_compass_and_straightedge.earliestOnPage: Hippias used a quadratrix in the fifth century BCE.

anc27_pythagorean_triples_tablet.what: Babylonian clay tablet with a sexagesimal table of Pythagorean triples.
anc27_pythagorean_triples_tablet.earliestOnPage: Estimated c. 1800 BC from handwriting style.

anc27_ancient_counting_board.what: Manual counting frame of sliding beads.
anc27_ancient_counting_board.earliestOnPage: The Sumerian abacus appeared between 2700 and 2300 BC (page statement).

anc27_greek_abacus_board.what: Manual counting frame of sliding beads.
anc27_greek_abacus_board.earliestOnPage: The Sumerian abacus appeared between 2700 and 2300 BC (page statement).

anc27_chinese_counting_rods.what: East Asian calculating bars forming a positional rod-numeral system.
anc27_chinese_counting_rods.earliestOnPage: Sunzi (c. 544-496 BCE) cited as mentioning their use.

anc27_ancient_square_root_algorithm.what: Numbers whose square equals a given number; computation methods and history.
anc27_ancient_square_root_algorithm.earliestOnPage: Tablet YBC 7289, 1800-1600 BC, shows square-root values in base 60.

anc27_ancient_astronomical_trigonometry.what: Greek astronomer and mathematician, considered founder of trigonometry; discoverer of precession.

anc27_early_sine_table.what: Sanskrit astronomical treatise by Aryabhata covering mathematics and astronomy.

anc27_archimedean_lever_proof.what: Greek mathematician, physicist, engineer and inventor (c. 287 - c. 212 BC).

anc27_indian_place_value_numerals.what: Base-ten positional numeral system with ten glyphs including zero, invented by Indian mathematicians.
anc27_indian_place_value_numerals.earliestOnPage: Bakhshali manuscript leaves, radiocarbon-dated 224-383 CE, use place value.

anc27_chinese_nine_chapters_diagram.page: The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art
anc27_chinese_nine_chapters_diagram.what: Anonymous Chinese mathematics text organising problems into nine chapters.
anc27_chinese_nine_chapters_diagram.earliestOnPage: Composition no later than 93 CE (Book of Later Han).

anc27_roman_surveyor_calculation_tablet.what: Roman surveying instrument with a rotating cross and plumb bobs for right angles and straight lines.
anc27_roman_surveyor_calculation_tablet.earliestOnPage: Not firmly dated; may have originated in Mesopotamia or Greece before the 4th century BC.

anc27_simple_lever_crane.what: Manual water-lifting device with a counterbalanced pole and bucket, used for irrigation.
anc27_simple_lever_crane.earliestOnPage: A cylinder seal depicting a shadoof, about 2200 BCE.

anc27_compound_pulley_block.what: Simple machine: a wheel on an axle guiding a rope to change direction or transmit power.
anc27_compound_pulley_block.earliestOnPage: Earliest evidence in Ancient Egypt, Twelfth Dynasty (1991-1802 BC).

anc27_wooden_windlass_hoist.what: Horizontal winch with a crank-turned barrel winding rope to move heavy weights.
anc27_wooden_windlass_hoist.earliestOnPage: Hero of Alexandria, about a century after Vitruvius (c. 28 BC), lists it among five simple machines.

anc27_capstan_hauling_device.what: Vertical-axle rotating machine multiplying crew force for hauling ropes and cables.

anc27_human_treadwheel_crane.what: Human-powered wooden lifting machine used in Roman and medieval construction.
anc27_human_treadwheel_crane.earliestOnPage: Haterii tombstone relief, late first century CE.

anc27_stone_lifting_shears.what: Lifting machine using a boom, hoist, cables and pulleys.
anc27_stone_lifting_shears.earliestOnPage: Shadoof, a Mesopotamian lever-lifting device, around 3000 BCE (page statement).

anc27_wooden_wedge_splitter.what: Triangular portable inclined plane, one of the six simple machines.

anc27_inclined_plane_ramp.what: Tilted flat surface used to raise or lower loads; a classical simple machine.
anc27_inclined_plane_ramp.earliestOnPage: Roman earth ramp at Masada, 72 AD.

anc27_ratchet_lift_mechanism.what: Mechanism permitting motion in one direction only, via pawl and teeth.

anc27_wooden_gear_pair.what: Rotating machine part whose teeth engage others to transmit torque.
anc27_wooden_gear_pair.earliestOnPage: Earliest surviving gears: 4th century BC China, Warring States.

anc27_right_angle_gear_drive.what: Rotating machine part whose teeth engage others to transmit torque.
anc27_right_angle_gear_drive.earliestOnPage: Earliest surviving gears: 4th century BC China, Warring States.

anc27_worm_gear_drive.what: Rotating machine part whose teeth engage others to transmit torque.
anc27_worm_gear_drive.earliestOnPage: Earliest surviving gears: 4th century BC China, Warring States.

anc27_ancient_water_clock_escapement.what: Timepiece measuring time by regulated liquid flow into or out of a marked vessel.
anc27_ancient_water_clock_escapement.earliestOnPage: Babylonian astronomical use c. 2000-1600 BC; oldest physical clock c. 1417-1379 BC, Egypt.

anc27_automaton_camshaft.what: Machine that runs operations or responds to preset instructions with little human input.
anc27_automaton_camshaft.earliestOnPage: Lie Zi text (c. 400 BCE) recounts Yan Shi presenting a life-size figure to King Mu of Zhou.

anc27_trip_hammer_camshaft.what: Shaft with cams converting rotary into reciprocating motion.
anc27_trip_hammer_camshaft.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (page: described by al-Jazari in 1206)

anc27_rotating_millstone_gear.what: Rotating machine part whose teeth engage others to transmit torque.
anc27_rotating_millstone_gear.earliestOnPage: Earliest surviving gears: 4th century BC China, Warring States.

anc27_ox_powered_rotary_mill.what: Mill that turns grain into flour; the machinery or the building.
anc27_ox_powered_rotary_mill.earliestOnPage: Strabo reports a water-powered grain mill at Cabira, Asia Minor, before 71 BC.

anc27_counterweight_door_mechanism.what: Weight that applies an opposing force to balance a mechanical system.

anc27_ancestor_memorial_stele.what: Upright stone or wooden slab erected as a monument, marker or memorial, often inscribed.
anc27_ancestor_memorial_stele.earliestOnPage: Old Kingdom mastaba stelae 2686-2181 BC; Nefertiabet funerary stele c. 2575 BC.

anc27_funerary_offering_bowl.what: Items buried with a body: belongings, afterlife supplies or offerings.
anc27_funerary_offering_bowl.earliestOnPage: Sima de los Huesos hominins, 430,000 years ago, with a handaxe suggested as a grave good.

anc27_temple_votive_figurine.what: Objects deposited in a sacred place for religious purposes without intent of recovery.
anc27_temple_votive_figurine.earliestOnPage: Olmec El Manati votive deposits, 1600-1200 BC.

anc27_stone_shrine_altar.what: Sacred space dedicated to a deity, ancestor or hero.

anc27_household_ancestor_tablet.what: Placard designating the seat of a deity or ancestor, used in East Asian ancestor veneration.

anc27_ceramic_burial_urn.what: Lidded vase with a narrow neck above a rounded body, often used for funerary ashes.
anc27_ceramic_burial_urn.earliestOnPage: Pottery urns from about 7000 BC at Jiahu, China.

anc27_carved_burial_sarcophagus.what: Stone coffin, usually above ground, often elaborately carved.
anc27_carved_burial_sarcophagus.earliestOnPage: Egyptian pharaohs of the 3rd dynasty, about 2686-2613 BC.

anc27_stone_boundary_sacred_marker.what: Robust physical markers, often stones, that identify the start of a land boundary or a change in its direction.

anc27_burial_grave_goods_chest.what: Items buried with a body: belongings, afterlife supplies or offerings.
anc27_burial_grave_goods_chest.earliestOnPage: Sima de los Huesos hominins, 430,000 years ago, with a handaxe suggested as a grave good.

anc27_ritual_libation_vessel.what: Ritual pouring of liquid as an offering to deities, spirits or the dead.
anc27_ritual_libation_vessel.earliestOnPage: Predynastic Egypt, Naqada I and II, c. 4000-3300 BCE.

anc27_shrine_incense_burner.what: Sacred space dedicated to a deity, ancestor or hero.

anc27_harvest_festival_offering_basket.what: Objects deposited in a sacred place for religious purposes without intent of recovery.
anc27_harvest_festival_offering_basket.earliestOnPage: Olmec El Manati votive deposits, 1600-1200 BC.

anc27_communal_ritual_calendar.what: Calendar keyed to the Sun, tracking seasons or the Sun place among the stars.

anc27_pilgrimage_route_marker.what: Journey to a holy place, often on foot.
anc27_pilgrimage_route_marker.earliestOnPage: not stated for antiquity (page: Origen, 3rd century).

anc27_temple_dedication_inscription.what: Upright stone or wooden slab erected as a monument, marker or memorial, often inscribed.
anc27_temple_dedication_inscription.earliestOnPage: Old Kingdom mastaba stelae 2686-2181 BC; Nefertiabet funerary stele c. 2575 BC.

anc27_bone_flute_with_fingerholes.what: Woodwind aerophone sounding when air flows across an opening.
anc27_bone_flute_with_fingerholes.earliestOnPage: Flutes from the Swabian Jura, Germany, about 53,000-45,000 years ago.

anc27_double_reed_aulos.what: Ancient Greek double-reed wind instrument, closer to an oboe than a flute.
anc27_double_reed_aulos.earliestOnPage: c. 2600 BC marble sculpture of an aulos player, Cycladic civilisation.

anc27_ancient_end_blown_flute.what: Woodwind aerophone sounding when air flows across an opening.
anc27_ancient_end_blown_flute.earliestOnPage: Flutes from the Swabian Jura, Germany, about 53,000-45,000 years ago.

anc27_reed_panpipes.what: Instrument of multiple closed pipes of gradually increasing length.

anc27_musical_conch_trumpet.what: Wind instrument made from a sea-snail shell, blown into its natural conical bore.
anc27_musical_conch_trumpet.earliestOnPage: Palestine conch instruments from approximately the third millennium BC (page statement).

anc27_ram_horn_shofar.what: Ancient musical horn, typically a ram horn, used in Jewish ritual.

anc27_lyre_sound_box.what: Stringed yoke-lute instrument whose strings attach to two arms and a crossbar.
anc27_lyre_sound_box.earliestOnPage: c. 2700 BC, archaeological sites in Mesopotamia.

anc27_ancient_harp_frame.what: Plucked stringed instrument with strings at an angle to the soundboard.
anc27_ancient_harp_frame.earliestOnPage: Chang harp introduced in Persia about 4000 BCE (earliest date on page).

anc27_wooden_lute_body.what: Plucked string instrument with a neck and deep hollow body.
anc27_wooden_lute_body.earliestOnPage: Page pushes existence of the lute back to c. 3100 BC.

anc27_plucked_kithara_instrument.what: Ancient Greek seven-stringed professional lyre-like instrument linked to Apollo.
anc27_plucked_kithara_instrument.earliestOnPage: Bronze figurine from Crete, c. 850 BCE (image caption only).

anc27_ancient_drum_frame.what: Percussion instrument (membranophone) with a drumhead stretched over a shell.
anc27_ancient_drum_frame.earliestOnPage: Alligator-skin drums in Neolithic China, 5500-2350 BC.

anc27_skin_head_hand_drum.what: Percussion instrument (membranophone) with a drumhead stretched over a shell.
anc27_skin_head_hand_drum.earliestOnPage: Alligator-skin drums in Neolithic China, 5500-2350 BC.

anc27_talking_drum_precursor.what: Percussion instrument (membranophone) with a drumhead stretched over a shell.
anc27_talking_drum_precursor.earliestOnPage: Alligator-skin drums in Neolithic China, 5500-2350 BC.

anc27_bronze_ritual_bell.what: Directly struck idiophone, usually a hollow cup-shaped body.
anc27_bronze_ritual_bell.earliestOnPage: Archaeological evidence from the 3rd millennium BCE, Yangshao culture, Neolithic China.

anc27_bronze_chime_set.what: Directly struck idiophone, usually a hollow cup-shaped body.
anc27_bronze_chime_set.earliestOnPage: Archaeological evidence from the 3rd millennium BCE, Yangshao culture, Neolithic China.

anc27_egyptian_arched_harp.what: Plucked stringed instrument with strings at an angle to the soundboard.
anc27_egyptian_arched_harp.earliestOnPage: Chang harp introduced in Persia about 4000 BCE (earliest date on page).

anc27_chinese_qin_zither.what: Plucked seven-string Chinese zither favoured by scholars.
anc27_chinese_qin_zither.earliestOnPage: Mentioned in Chinese writings nearly 3,000 years old; examples in tombs about 2,500 years old.

anc27_andean_terrace_retaining_wall.what: Rigid structure holding back soil so ground sits at different levels.

anc27_andean_waru_waru_field.what: Pre-Hispanic Andean raised-field farming pairing raised beds with irrigation canals.
anc27_andean_waru_waru_field.earliestOnPage: Radiocarbon dates from associated sites indicate use as early as 1000 BC.

anc27_andean_quipu_knot_record.what: Record-keeping device of knotted cords used in the central Andes, most prominently by the Inca.
anc27_andean_quipu_knot_record.earliestOnPage: Claimed proto-quipu at Caral c. 3000-1800 BCE, not yet thoroughly evaluated; undisputed evidence c. 600-1000 CE.

anc27_nazca_underground_puquio.what: More than 40 aqueducts near Nazca, Peru, built by the Nazca culture as part of puquio water systems.
anc27_nazca_underground_puquio.earliestOnPage: About 1,500 years ago (approximate; no specific date).

anc27_andean_rope_suspension_bridge.what: Primitive bridge whose deck rests on two parallel cables anchored at each end.
anc27_andean_rope_suspension_bridge.earliestOnPage: Oldest known suspension bridge reported from Central American ruins, 7th century (page statement).

anc27_mesoamerican_chinampa_canal.what: Mesoamerican raised-field technique using artificial islands on shallow lake beds in the Valley of Mexico.
anc27_mesoamerican_chinampa_canal.earliestOnPage: Earliest securely dated fields 1150-1350 CE (Culhuacan reportedly c. 1100 CE).

anc27_olmec_basalt_monument.what: Basalt stone sculptures of human heads, characteristic of Olmec civilisation.
anc27_olmec_basalt_monument.earliestOnPage: Heads from at least 900 BCE; San Lorenzo heads buried by 900 BC.

anc27_mesoamerican_cacao_grinding_metate.what: Quern-type ground stone tool for grinding grain and seeds, used with a hand-held mano.
anc27_mesoamerican_cacao_grinding_metate.earliestOnPage: Use estimated to begin in Mexico c. 5000-3000 BC.

anc27_ethiopian_highland_terrace.what: Flat step-like platform cut into hills to create farmland and reduce erosion and runoff.
anc27_ethiopian_highland_terrace.earliestOnPage: Levant terrace farming as early as the 4th millennium BCE.

anc27_saqiya_pot_chain_guide_wheel.what: Animal-powered water-lifting wheel with buckets or scoops, used mainly for irrigation.
anc27_saqiya_pot_chain_guide_wheel.earliestOnPage: Faiyum saqiya dated to the 3rd century BC.

anc27_meroitic_iron_smelting_furnace.what: Extracting metal from ore using heat and a reducing agent; impurities leave as gas or slag.
anc27_meroitic_iron_smelting_furnace.earliestOnPage: Copper smelting evidence 5500-5000 BC at Plocnik and Belovode, Serbia.

anc27_west_african_earthen_granary.what: Above-ground building for storing harvested grain or seeds, protecting them from pests, floods, and weather while helping prevent mold.
anc27_west_african_earthen_granary.earliestOnPage: Oldest found date to 9500 BC, Pre-Pottery Neolithic A settlements in the Jordan Valley.

anc27_southeast_asian_bronze_dong_son_dr.what: Ancient bronze drum of the Dong Son culture, Red River Delta, used as instrument and worship object.
anc27_southeast_asian_bronze_dong_son_dr.earliestOnPage: Production dated to about 600 BCE or earlier.

anc27_mayan_elevated_sacbe_road.what: Raised paved road built by the Maya connecting temples, plazas and cities.

anc27_maya_limestone_reservoir.what: Human-made store of water, typically an enlarged lake behind a dam.
anc27_maya_limestone_reservoir.earliestOnPage: Circa 3000 BC, volcanic craters in Arabia served as irrigation reservoirs (page statement).

anc27_aksumite_monumental_obelisk.what: Kingdom in the Horn of Africa and South Arabia, c. 1st century to c. 960 AD, centred on Axum.
anc27_aksumite_monumental_obelisk.earliestOnPage: Nafas Mawca tomb, third century AD, covered by a single stone block (not explicitly a stele).
